data.description:
## Why
`c11 --window <id> <command>` focuses that window before the command runs. Fleet commands then pull the operator's key window around while agents work. Backlog item: C5.

## Evidence
- c11: `CLI/c11.swift:1732-1736` on origin/main (0ff8887e5e) stores the global `--window` value. `:1951-1953` then sends `window.focus` before the command switch. The comment above it says the focus exists so commands route correctly.
- c11: many commands already suppress the `CMUX_WORKSPACE_ID` fallback when `windowId != nil` (for example `new-split` at `:2253` and `identify` at `:1978`). They do not all resolve workspace and tab refs inside that window. `normalizeWindowHandle(...) ?? windowId` at `:1952` still forwards an unparsed value into `window.focus`.
- c11: focus is a policy, not a side effect of routing. `Sources/TerminalController.swift:502-506` allows in-app focus mutation only for methods in `focusIntentV2Methods`. `window.focus` is one of those (`Sources/SocketHandlers/WindowHandlers.swift:21`). A command that is not a focus command must not call it.
- Upstream: cmux #4211 (`dea2f64684`). `--window` becomes a `window_id` param. Other refs resolve inside that window. An unparsable `window_id` is rejected. The env workspace fallback is off when `--window` is set.
- Research: `upstream-triage/c11-1.0/06-grab-list.md` §1g. Fable and Astra both mark it core. Astra raised it from S to M because deleting the focus call without threading scope still routes to the wrong window. The backlog label is S. Plan the full routing fix. The extra work is the ref scope, not a new feature.

## Scope
In: stop sending `window.focus` from the global `--window` flag. Pass `window_id` on the command's own socket call. Resolve workspace, area, and tab refs inside that window. An unparsable or unknown window id is an error, and the key window does not change. When `--window` is set, do not fall back to `CMUX_WORKSPACE_ID` or the focused workspace.
Out: changing which commands are focus-intent (`workspace.select`, `surface.focus`, `window.focus` itself, and the rest of the existing list). The focus-allowance stack race on C11-140 section A. `settings.open` activation, also on C11-140. Per-command `--window` help that already means "this command focuses" stays. `focus-window` still focuses.

## Approach
Delete the pre-dispatch `window.focus` at `:1951-1953`. Thread the parsed window id into the commands that already take a window override, and add `window_id` to the v2 params of the commands operators actually run from another window: `send`, `read-screen`, `tree`, `new-tab`, `new-split`, `new-area`, `list-workspaces`, and `workspace.select` only when that command is the one being invoked. `workspace.select` may focus because it is focus-intent. The others must not. Resolution of `workspace:N` and `tab:N` uses the window's own refs. If a ref is not in that window, return `not_found` rather than scanning other windows. Search skills and `tests_v2` for a caller that depends on the focus side effect, and update it to call `focus-window` or `window.focus` explicitly. Update the c11 skill's focus-policy paragraph.

## Acceptance criteria
1. With two windows open and window A key, `c11 --window <B> read-screen --tab <tab in B>` returns B's screen, and A is still key afterwards. Confirm with the frontmost-window id before and after.
2. `c11 --window not-a-window read-screen` exits non-zero, names the bad id, and does not change the key window.
3. `c11 --window <B> send --tab <tab in A>` does not deliver to A's tab. It errors `not_found` (or the equivalent), and A's screen is unchanged.
4. `c11 focus-window --window <B>` still focuses B. `c11 --window <B> workspace select <ws in B>` may change in-app selection. It still must not be required for criterion 1.
5. A grep of the CLI dispatch shows `window.focus` is sent only from `focus-window` and from other commands whose documented purpose is focus.

## Validation
A `tests_v2` script against a tagged build that opens or uses two windows if the harness can, otherwise a computer-use pass for criteria 1 through 3. Criterion 5 is review of the dispatch plus the test that calls a non-focus command. No soak. This removes a focus side effect. It must not add work to `WindowTerminalHostView.hitTest`.

## Dependencies
None inside this workstream. Neighbor: C11-140 section A (focus-allowance stack, `settings.open`). Do not take that work on. C1's key check is a different seam. Land them so `CLI/c11.swift` conflicts are expected and small.

## Risks
Typing latency: none on the keystroke path. Main thread: `window.focus` today is a socket round trip before every `--window` command. Removing it is the point. Do not replace it with `NSApp.activate`. Doctrine: routing is not focus. Localization: the bad-id error uses `String(localized:)`. Six-locale fill is X1. Public repo: the skill should say `--window` scopes and does not raise. Callers who wanted the raise call `focus-window`.

Size: S–M. Tier: P1. Doctrine check: a routing flag does not steal the key window.
data.title: Scope --window without focusing that window

data.body:
Owner validation for C11-283 at clean head 50fa043ece804bfd820eb94ddf91ad9b45fe7e4a, base 43529df178a9cd8817fc092896efd2f3fcd63df5, branch c11-1.0/C11-283-window-scope.

Tagged Debug build c11-283-window-scope compiled successfully through remote-build.sh. The manifest reports dirty=false and the real native executable SHA256 matches f3b154dc4c396ea5dea5d70d340352ef12c4cbc17b0c4452681428098ca6e8a1. Native capability commit stamps/sha_match are null; exact-head attribution uses the clean build manifest and executable digest instead. Native XCTest was not run by the owner.

The final packaged CLI passed 94 subprocess/fake-socket behavioral cases: UUID/ref/index scope, duplicate local indexes, caller-env suppression, scoped reads/creation/metadata, invalid window tokens, foreign sends, legacy notification/sidebar routing, attention admission, snapshots/restores, config routing, area operations, move source/destination behavior and three tree scopes with modern/ignoring/unsupported server modes. Fixtures mutate observable state and assert no foreign delivery/mutation; they do not inspect source text.

The real tagged app passed 25 checks on one verified 1920x1080 remote display. A PID-scoped UI AXRaise established key A. Reads addressed B and returned B's sentinel; A stayed key. Invalid/empty windows rejected without focus changes. A foreign-tab send returned not_found and its sentinel appeared in neither terminal. Ambient caller tabs could not admit send/send-key. New-tab, title/description, config default/new-workspace placement, invalid config refs, source-preserving moves, explicit cross-window moves and tree scopes passed. The feature was advertised at version 1. Own app Quit menu click returned 0; the later confirmation lookup found no process (return 1); process exit was verified. No screenshot or video claim is made.

Evidence: art_01M3XYA44QJ6XHH9GDPZ9410BH. Synthetic labels only; no home paths, account/machine names, prompts, emails or agent session IDs. No guest was created by this lane.

Three fresh-context static review rounds found routing gaps; owner repaired them, including the final move seam, and the final binary passed the expanded fixture and native checks. The Orchestrator's independent review remains pending. GitHub CI is queued/running on the draft PR and will be watched; no green CI claim yet. Only the Merge Captain syncs installed skills after landing.

Validator scenario:
1. Build merged main with a fresh tagged app. Confirm capabilities.features advertises window.route_without_focus version 1; use that app's packaged CLI and owned socket throughout.
2. Create two windows A/B with synthetic workspace names. Set neutral shell prompts (PS1='$ ', or PROMPT='$ '), clear scrollback/display, and print distinct synthetic screen markers. Use PID-scoped UI setup to make A key; record window.list key flags before each test. The existing focus-window handler selects the active manager and orders a window forward; it does not guarantee changing macOS key window.
3. From a caller context whose workspace/tab env IDs belong to A, run global --window B read-screen targeting B by UUID/ref and numeric index. Expect B text, scoped routing, and A still key. List/create helpers must operate only within B and preserve key A.
4. Try unknown, absent and empty window tokens. Expect nonzero errors echoing the unknown token and unchanged key A. Send with B scope and explicit A tab must return not_found, with no sentinel in A or B. Send/send-key without an explicit tab must reject the A caller-env fallback and deliver nothing.
5. Exercise scoped sidebar/notification helpers and explicit title/description targets from caller A; only B changes. Foreign workspace/tab UUIDs must fail before a legacy write. Config launch with default/new-workspace placement must land in B; unknown explicit workspace/area refs must reject.
6. Put a tab in a nonselected B workspace. A B-scoped index-only move must preserve its source workspace/area. An explicit command-local destination window A and workspace A must transfer that B source to A. Foreign source/anchor/area handles without an explicit permitted destination must fail before mutation.
7. Compare B-scoped tree default, tree --window and tree --all. Default includes B's selected workspace only; window/all include B's workspaces only. Existing explicit focus-window B must still select B's active manager, observable through current-window, without relying on a macOS key-window change.
8. Inspect owned layout for readable areas. Quit only the tagged PID, prove process/socket teardown, and delete the owned remote tag/build directories and any owned guest. Keep unrelated sessions and guests untouched.

Runtime closeout: the owned tagged app is gone. Its remote source/artifact tag directory and tagged DerivedData directory were deleted after proof retrieval. This lane created zero guests; unrelated guests were left untouched. Draft PR #525 is mergeable at 50fa043ece804bfd820eb94ddf91ad9b45fe7e4a; exact-head CI remains in flight and is being watched.

Verdict: FAIL

Reviewed head 50fa043ece804bfd820eb94ddf91ad9b45fe7e4a against merge-base 43529df178a9cd8817fc092896efd2f3fcd63df5. Detached checkout is clean. Read the complete seven-file diff, ticket, plan, validation comment ev_01M3XYDAGFZH2D14W8DAAC6H7B, artifact art_01M3XYA44QJ6XHH9GDPZ9410BH, required doctrine, and relevant unchanged dispatch/resolution handlers. Static review only: no reviewer builds, tests, or UI runs. PR head matches; CI still has queued/running checks, so no green-CI claim.

Blocking

1. CLI/c11.swift:2075-2083, 2842-2856, 12844-12846: replacing the global focus prelude with SocketClient.scopedWindow leaves legacy routing commands on the active window. With active/key window A, B containing a different selected workspace, and each workspace having movable tabs, `c11 --window B drag-tab-to-split --tab 0 right` still sends the unchanged v1 `drag_surface_to_split 0 right`. Sources/TerminalController.swift:7645-7683 resolves index 0 inside the active manager's selected workspace and splits A's tab. Likewise `c11 --window B default-agent launch` sends unscoped `default_agent launch`; Sources/TerminalController.swift:9612-9657 selects the active manager and launches in A. These are concrete violations of the requested window-scoped routing, not focus-intent changes. Smallest fix: carry the resolved target through these legacy routes (or use an equivalent scoped endpoint while preserving their behavior), without restoring window.focus. Include refresh-tabs in that same legacy-route pass: its handler at TerminalController.swift:9297 also uses the active selected workspace. Add behavioral cases proving only B changes, with A remaining key.

2. CLI/c11.swift:14823-14826 and 14868-14882: explicit foreign workspace selection becomes a successful fallback. `c11 --window B tree --workspace <workspace-in-A>` passes the foreign UUID/ref through normalizeWorkspaceHandle. The actual system.tree handler finds A's workspace globally (Sources/SocketHandlers/SystemHandlers.swift:513-531); filtering removes A and triggers the newly added legacy fallback. That fallback sends workspace.list with window B and workspace A. The real workspace.list handler (WorkspaceHandlers.swift:80-109) lists every workspace in B and does not validate/filter workspace_id. The CLI then returns all of B successfully, instead of rejecting the foreign workspace. The same fallback against a server without system.tree returns all B workspaces even for an explicit single B workspace. Smallest fix: validate explicit tree workspace membership in the scoped window and filter fallback results to that resolved workspace. Correct the fake workspace.list semantics at tests/test_cli_window_scope.py:333-338, then cover foreign-workspace rejection and a nonselected B workspace in both native and fallback tree modes. Current numbered Validator step 7 covers only default/window/all, so it misses this case.

3. CLI/c11.swift:1438, 1454, 1459, 8893: four newly added user-visible scope errors are bare English CLIError strings. For example, a foreign move/flag target emits `not_found: Tab not found in scoped window` without any String(localized:) call, so the six-locale translation pass cannot supply its translated message. This violates the explicit localization gate; it is separate from deferring translations to C11-291. Smallest fix: wrap the new messages in stable localization keys with English defaultValue, preserving the machine-readable not_found prefix. No hand-authored translations are requested here.

Non-blocking

None. The feature is enabled and consumed through the typed registry, the global window.focus prelude is removed, and the tests execute a CLI subprocess with observable state assertions rather than grepping source. The config.launch window forwarding is consistent with the downstream agent.launch resolver. No typing-path, focus-intent-list, agent-config-write, or public-data disclosure change was found in this diff.

Runtime proof still required

Batch validation is accepted for this low-risk ticket. Deferred runtime proof alone is not a failure, and this review does not require an extra pre-merge UI run. The owner reports 94 CLI fixture cases and 25 tagged native checks; the supplied artifact records those results and build identity, but I did not independently execute them.

After repairs, Atlas CI must pass the corrected CLI fixture on the reviewed revision. The Validator's numbered steps 1-8 are suitable for the original read/send/no-focus criteria, including using real key-window flags and preserving the existing explicit focus-window semantics. Extend steps 3/7 with the legacy mutations and explicit tree workspace cases in findings 1/2. Include a previously live, then closed window handle and a no-global-window control. Run that expanded scenario on the fresh packaged merged-main app in the authorized batch, proving unchanged key A, no mutation/delivery outside B, foreign-target errors, version-1 feature advertisement, and owned-app teardown. Do not treat the existing owner checks as proof of these uncovered cases.

Repair round 1 for blocking review ev_01M3XYQPF1QM1AJQYZ36MYV1P6. One repair commit: 15df94ffc95a324e49ad424d4c0bbe2c400031a9, pushed to c11-1.0/C11-283-window-scope. Draft PR: https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/c11/pull/525.

Legacy drag-tab-to-split, refresh-tabs and default-agent launch now carry the resolved workspace through their v1 handlers. The server resolves its owning manager without window.focus or changing the active manager. Existing-tab launch scopes cwd lookup and delivery to that workspace. Explicit tree workspace selectors are validated inside the global window before native lookup; the fallback filters workspace.list enumeration to that workspace. The fixture now models the real list semantics. Malformed explicit tab tokens reject before mutation. All new scope errors use localized English keys.

Exact clean head compiled through remote-build.sh on tagged Debug build c11-283-window-scope, with no overlay. Native executable SHA256: c6b5d0f4b14a979d0d66c5f40a0fdc10dd0a4f1f6409ee3102d7f02b7a512ca2. Attribution uses the clean manifest and executable digest; server commit and sha_match remain null. Owner native XCTest was not run.

119 packaged CLI subprocess/fake-socket cases passed, including all three scoped legacy mutations, foreign and malformed legacy target rejection, unscoped controls, stale closed-window rejection, and explicit nonselected/foreign workspace UUID/ref trees on native, ignoring-scope and unsupported-tree server modes. Tests check observable state and no window.focus request.

35 real tagged-app checks passed, including legacy drag/default launch only changing B with A still key, refresh returning B's terminal count, unscoped controls retaining active A, native explicit nonselected B trees returning exactly one workspace, and foreign A workspace UUID/ref rejection. Existing target tab/area selection semantics are preserved. The run used only its owned tagged app; it quit and its exit was verified. After the UI stop instruction, read-only process checks confirmed zero owned tagged apps locally and remotely; no further UI launch occurred. No screenshot/video claim is made.

Sanitized evidence: art_01M3Y03KE1M5KKEQ3RZKF3D3T7. Fresh static CLI review found no remaining defects after two owner repairs before the single commit. Additional server observations concerned preexisting target tab/area selection behavior, which the stored cut preserves; runtime checks proved no active-window change. Independent Orchestrator review remains pending. Exact-head GitHub CI is queued/running; the previous head's checks passed. No new-head green claim.

English keys for C11-291: cli.window.scope.workspaceNotFound, cli.window.scope.tabNotFound, cli.window.scope.areaNotFound, cli.window.scope.workspaceTabNotFound, socket.workspace.invalid, socket.workspace.not_found. No installed skill copies changed. No guest was created. Owned remote tag/build directories are deleted after evidence retrieval.

Validator scenario:
1. Build a fresh tagged merged-main app; advertise window.route_without_focus version 1. Use its packaged CLI and owned socket. Take the UI slot before any window launch/interaction and obey the 20-minute cap.
2. Create synthetic windows A/B, with one terminal in A and at least two in B, plus a nonselected second workspace in B. Use neutral prompts and synthetic screen markers. Establish A as key through approved UI setup; keep A the active manager. Record key flags, tab IDs and area IDs.
3. With caller workspace/tab environment belonging to A, globally scope read-screen, new-tab and metadata commands to B. Expect B routing and A still key. Unknown/empty/stale windows reject; scoped send/send-key cannot inherit caller A's tab. A foreign-tab send rejects and delivers no sentinel anywhere.
4. Globally scope drag-tab-to-split, refresh-tabs and default-agent launch to B. Configure only the tagged app's custom agent to a synthetic printf command, restoring it afterward. Expect B's area/tab counts to change, refresh to return B's terminal count, and A's tab/area IDs and key flag unchanged. Foreign and malformed tab selectors reject before v1 mutation.
5. Run those legacy commands without global scope as controls. Expect their existing active-A behavior and no changes to B. Preserve each command's existing target tab/area selection semantics.
6. Run B-scoped tree --workspace with the nonselected B workspace UUID and ref. Expect exactly that one workspace. A workspace UUID/ref must reject, preserving key A. Repeat against the executable fixture's native, ignoring-scope and unsupported-tree modes to prove fallback filtering. Close B and retry its old handle; expect rejection without A mutation.
7. Repeat scoped config default/new-workspace placement, source-preserving index moves and explicit cross-window destination moves. Default tree includes selected B workspace; tree --window/--all include B workspaces only. Existing focus-window still selects the requested active manager.
8. Quit only the owned tagged app through its socket, verify process/socket teardown, restore temporary app settings, and delete owned tag/build directories and any owned guests. Do not synthesize input or launch windows without the UI slot.

Verdict: PASS

Round 2 delta review only: 50fa043ece804bfd820eb94ddf91ad9b45fe7e4a..15df94ffc95a324e49ad424d4c0bbe2c400031a9. Exact detached head and clean checkout verified; PR head matches. Reviewed all four changed files and the directly touched resolution/parsing paths. No reviewer builds, tests, or UI runs.

Blocking

None. All three prior findings are resolved:
1. Legacy drag-tab-to-split, refresh-tabs, and default-agent launch carry a resolved workspace through their v1 handlers. The server resolves its owning manager without changing the active manager. Existing-tab launch constrains both cwd lookup and delivery to that workspace; unscoped paths retain their prior manager selection.
2. Explicit tree workspaces are validated inside the global window before dispatch. Fallback enumeration is filtered to the resolved workspace. The fixture now models the real workspace.list semantics and checks foreign UUID/ref rejection plus a single nonselected B workspace across all three tree modes.
3. The four reported English scope errors now use String(localized:) keys with English defaults and retain the not_found prefix. New server workspace errors are localized too.

Non-blocking

Evidence wording discrepancy: validation comment ev_01M3Y05PD1W9W2G6MMG3F20RDJ says server commit/sha_match remain null; artifact art_01M3Y03KE1M5KKEQ3RZKF3D3T7 instead records server_commit=15df94ffc and reported_sha_match=true. Both identify the same full reviewed head and executable digest. This does not reopen a code finding; owner can correct the comment for consistency.

Runtime proof still required

Owner evidence reports 119 packaged CLI behavioral cases and 35 tagged-app checks, including the repaired legacy routes and native explicit tree scope. These are owner results, not independently rerun here. Updated numbered Validator steps 1-8 adequately cover the three repairs, unscoped controls, closed-window rejection, key-window preservation, and owned-app teardown. Run them on merged main in the authorized batch. Deferred batch proof is not blocking. Exact-head CI is not yet fully green and remains a separate landing gate.

BLOCKED C11-283 PR #525 at reviewed head 15df94ffc95a324e49ad424d4c0bbe2c400031a9 against current main 531908b8d5cab3d8d6491532287b4f7dc23c45f8. Exact-head Astra delta PASS ev_01M3Y0A9KEM1RN7MRVCG3MJQCB verified; validation ev_01M3Y05PD1W9W2G6MMG3F20RDJ records packaged fixture and tagged-app checks, with remaining numbered batch scenarios.
Actual merge-tree and GitHub CONFLICTING identify Sources/CapabilityFeatures.swift, skills/c11/SKILL.md and skills/c11/references/api.md. Merge handoff at a9967182509b3dfcfea487f659f47b01271a2ada on draft PR https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/c11/pull/525. Merged origin/main 531908b8d5cab3d8d6491532287b4f7dc23c45f8 into the existing branch; no rebase or force push.

Merge handoff at 6bc28658e554acd9cbf597f9fc032bf4b6b093be on draft PR https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/c11/pull/525. Merged origin/main 85f33041c525156ad31b651f45e425ea0e24a7ae into the existing branch; one push, no rebase or force push.

Resolution logic: the shared send/send-tab/paste dispatch uses C11-281's parsed workspace/tab and preserves C11-283's caller-environment suppression under global --window or an explicit workspace. Admission checks the effective surfaceArg, not an environment tab that was excluded from routing. send-tab additionally requires its explicit tab flag. Raw/stdin/no-submit handling remains C11-281's implementation. Both skill texts are retained: background window scope and send modes/delivery state. Registry entries merged automatically and remain enabled.

Exact clean merged-head tagged Debug compile-check passed on the remote worker through remote-build.sh with no overlay. Its packaged CLI passed 128 window-scope fake-socket cases, including nine added merged-send cases: send-tab, paste and send --raw each route an explicit B target without changing A, reject caller-A admission under B scope, and reject foreign A tab refs without mutation. Raw/paste payload escapes and no-submit survive the merge. Harness invokes the real compiled CLI and asserts observable fixture state/no window.focus, without inspecting source text.

Sanitized evidence: art_01M3Y17PFRY2QMKVQ6ZPP55HYV. No other tests ran. No app launch or UI work was performed. Previous 35 native checks remain evidence at implementation head 15df94ffc95a324e49ad424d4c0bbe2c400031a9 only; no new native runtime claim. Exact-head CI is pending and remains the Merge Captain's gate.

Validator scenario: retain the numbered scenario in ev_01M3Y05PD1W9W2G6MMG3F20RDJ. Extend its scoped send step to send-tab, paste --no-submit and send --raw --no-submit: explicit B targets must receive exactly the supplied raw payload for raw/paste; missing explicit targets under --window B must reject even with caller A's environment, and explicit A targets must reject without delivery. A stays key. Take the UI slot before launching/operating a tagged window; no owner UI rerun was authorized here.

Owned remote compile-check tag/build directories were deleted after the CLI run. Installed skills untouched. C11-289 remains paused on its pushed clean branch with no PR. Stopping per Orchestrator instruction.

Verdict: PASS

Narrow merge review of 6bc28658e554acd9cbf597f9fc032bf4b6b093be (parents a996718250 C11-283, 85f33041c5 C11-281 / main). Read-only. Conflict resolution only, from `git show --remerge-diff`. No builds, tests, or subagents.

Blocking

None.

The resolution keeps both sides' named behavior.

1. C11-283 scope. `CLI/c11.swift:3182-3188` builds `surfaceArg` from the explicit tab, and uses the caller tab only when both `--workspace` and `--window` are absent. The guard admits that effective target. `send-tab` also requires its own `--tab`. Global `--window` still resolves once and stores `scopedWindow` (`CLI/c11.swift:2133-2141`). `focus-window` is still the focus command (`CLI/c11.swift:2238-2243`). A numeric workspace is listed inside that window (`CLI/c11.swift:5407-5413`). `sendV2` stamps `window_id` on `tab.send_text` (`CLI/c11.swift:1390-1396`). A tab that is not in the window comes back `not_found` from that scoped call.

2. C11-281 send parsing. `Sources/SendTextParse.swift` matches 85f33041c5. Unknown flags throw inside `parse` before the text join (`Sources/SendTextParse.swift:51-54`, join at `:70-72`). `parse` runs before connect (`CLI/c11.swift:1855-1860`). `-` selects stdin; the bytes are read after admission (`CLI/c11.swift:3190-3191`). `--raw` returns the text unchanged (`Sources/SendTextParse.swift:90`) and sets `preserve_newlines` (`CLI/c11.swift:3189-3193`). `submit` defaults to true (`Sources/SendTextParse.swift:17`) and is copied into the socket params (`CLI/c11.swift:3192`).
